id: Stable identifier returned by the engine. Treat it as opaque.
kind: Resource or operation kind. Use one of the listed values, not a display label.
name: Human-readable name. It is not necessarily unique.
external_id: Your stable identifier for this person, agent or service within the workspace.
metadata: Application-supplied JSON metadata. Do not put credentials here.
disabled: Whether the identity is disabled; disabled identities cannot retain normal access.
agent: Stable agent external ID when enrolling; an Agent object in a Session response.
agent_id: Logical agent identity ID, shared by its runtime instances.
instance_id: Exact connected runtime ID, separate from the logical agent identity.
instances: Runtime connections and their observed presence.
parent_id: Optional parent agent identity for a deliberately bounded enrollment.
capabilities: Application-declared runtime capabilities. This does not grant contact permission.
presence: Observed runtime presence: connected, stale or offline.
progress: Explicit application-reported progress metadata; not automatic model telemetry.
token: Bearer credential. Save in protected server-side storage and never expose it in browser code or logs.
expires_at: Expiry timestamp. Ordinary communication has no implicit deadline (represented as 9999-01-01T00:00:00Z). Bound action approvals default to seven days; explicit expiry must be within ninety days. Local wait timeout never changes it.
body: Message or request content, bounded to 32 KiB of UTF-8 bytes.
title: Optional short label. A normal message does not require a title.
target: Target kind and stable ID. Choose a new target or an existing conversation, not both.
targets: Explicit targets for a private batch or shared chat. These have different audience semantics.
target_kind: Kind of identity or managed resource matched by the rule.
target_id: Stable ID or explicitly supported wildcard of the rule's target.
conversation_id: Canonical conversation ID. Use it to continue the same authorized history.
request_id: Canonical durable request ID. This is not a worker delivery ID.
message_id: Canonical message ID for deduplication and correlation.
sender_id: Identity that sent the message, independent of the delivering channel.
requester_id: Identity that opened the requested decision.
requester_instance_id: Runtime that initiated the request, when applicable.
responder_instance_id: Runtime that supplied the final response, when applicable.
recipient_id: Intended individual identity for the delivery or event projection.
actor_id: Identity responsible for the canonical event.
principal_id: Person, agent or service identity ID. This is an API term, not a separate product entity.
subject_id: Identity or directory group receiving a policy-role assignment.
subject_kind: principal for an individual identity, or group for a directory group.
choices: Optional exact answer strings. A chosen answer must match an offered value.
answer: JSON response value; for choices, the selected exact string.
outcome: Typed final result: answered; approved/denied; or completed/failed/rejected according to request kind.
state: Lifecycle state. Read the resource-specific enum; request and execution states differ.
version: Current optimistic-concurrency version. Read the object before a guarded change; a stale version conflicts.
response: Recorded final typed decision, absent while pending.
action: Optional exact bound-action descriptor for the advanced execution contract.
action_name: Optional action-name constraint; not required for ordinary approval communication.
executor_id: Identity allowed to redeem the exact approved action.
resource: Customer-defined resource identifier. The engine does not control the external resource.
resource_version: Customer-defined version fence that the external tool must also enforce.
operation_key: Stable identity of the external business operation, separate from the HTTP retry key.
arguments: JSON action arguments covered by the exact approval binding.
result: Executor-reported JSON result. It is not independent proof of an external effect.
reuse_direct: Opt into reusing exact authorized two-person history. False by default; does not merge shared chats.
preview_token: Dispatch preview token. A stale audience or route requires a fresh preview.
mentions: Addressing metadata for existing chat participants. It does not narrow audience or grant authority.
start: Inclusive Unicode code-point offset of the mention, not a byte or UTF-16 index.
end: Exclusive Unicode code-point offset of the mention.
attachment_ids: IDs of staged private drafts to claim in the initial operation; at most five.
file_name: Safe file name shown with the attachment.
media_type: Declared media type, for example application/pdf.
size: File length in bytes, from 1 byte through 5 MiB.
sha256: SHA-256 digest of the stored file bytes.
shared: True for a shared chat, distinct from private histories created by a batch.
participants: Current participants in the authorized history projection.
past_participants: Former participant metadata visible to the caller; does not restore their access.
manager_id: Manager identity for a person, or current shared-chat manager according to the resource.
history_start: Earliest event boundary disclosed to this participant.
last_activity_at: Most recent conversation activity timestamp; used for recency ordering.
last_preview: Last visible message preview; hidden history is not exposed through previews.
messages: Canonical message records in this response, not worker delivery envelopes.
message_count: Number of canonical messages accepted in the compact receipt; no bodies returned.
operation: Requested operation, with values defined by that endpoint.
member: Whether the current identity belongs to this directory group.
members: Directory-group or chat member identity IDs. Membership never substitutes for contact authority.
members_complete: Whether the visible member list is complete rather than permission-projected.
purpose: Directory group purpose: contacts, team or agent_role. This is separate from policy roles.
role_id: Policy role ID used by a binding; not the agent_role directory-group ID.
rules: Directional permission rules granted by this policy role.
conditions: Optional descriptor/time/amount constraints on the rule.
config: Provider-specific configuration. Use the catalog's actual fields; secret material is separately protected.
secret: Write-only provider secret. Omitted from ordinary read/setup responses.
secret_configured: Whether protected secret material is configured, without returning it.
enabled: Whether this configured connection is enabled.
address: Provider-native destination address for a linked identity.
mode: primary, copy or fallback routing mode.
priority: Routing order within the applicable mode; lower numeric values are considered first.
remove: True to remove the specified role binding rather than add it.
delivery_id: Transport delivery record ID. Different attempts can refer to the same canonical message/request.
attempts: Delivery attempt count or recorded attempt evidence, as defined by this response.
generation: Current inbox lease generation. Ack must echo this generation.
payload: Canonical message/request information inside a delivery envelope.
last_error: Latest safe delivery error, not a successful execution report.
sequence: Monotonically ordered canonical event sequence. Checkpoint after application processing.
data: Event-specific JSON data. Full events contain the canonical payload; summary mode is smaller.
key: Stable idempotency key or shared-answer lookup key according to the endpoint.
shared_key: Explicit reusable-answer key; reuse also requires exact matching question context and current authority.
audience: Explicit identities allowed to reuse the published informational answer.
valid_until: Reusable-answer expiry timestamp; omission defaults to 24 hours.
source_answer_id: Published answer used as response provenance.
source_invalidated: Whether the source informational answer has since been invalidated.
reuse_method: How an existing informational answer was reused.
reuse_reason: Recorded reason or provenance for reuse.
overseer: Whether OSS Coordinator is enabled in this workspace. The wire name is retained for compatibility.
overseer_configured: Whether the engine has a configured Coordinator provider; not the enablement switch.
prompt: Instruction to Coordinator. The engine supplies only currently permitted specialist context.
context_agent_ids: Agent IDs included in the current permitted plan context.
sources: Authorized specialist context used for this plan, not omniscient agent execution state.
fresh: Whether the reported runtime evidence is current.
automatic: True when Coordinator delegated without a separate review step.
requires_confirmation: Whether this saved plan needs explicit confirmation before dispatch.
instructions: Per-agent communication instructions, when different specialists need different tasks.
summary: Plan explanation or status answer, as defined by its operation.
summary_error: Safe model-summary error. Existing durable instructions remain separately inspectable.
dispatches: Attributed conversation/request IDs created by a confirmed or automatic plan.
replies: Specialist requested decisions visible to the current caller.
reply_summary: Model-generated summary of the authorized replies, including pending/missing evidence.
reply_digest: Digest identifying the reply evidence used by the summary.
previous_plan_id: Optional prior plan belonging to the caller for continuing permitted context.
blocking: Explicit requester-declared agent dependency. Ordinary pending questions are not automatically blocking.
email: Person email address. An address alone does not prove identity or decision authority.
code: Stable API error code for programmatic handling.
error: Error envelope with code and message; do not treat it as a successful result.
required: Whether this provider field must be configured.
fields: Provider setup field definitions with types, requirements and safe constraints.
identity: Provider identity-linking requirements or current evidence.
setup_modes: Supported setup methods; use only advertised modes.
builtin: Whether the capability is provided by the engine without a provider installation.
file_mode: Actual attachment transport behavior for the provider.
web_continuation: Whether the conversation can continue in the workspace.
web_continuation_supported: Whether this provider supports a workspace continuation link.
native_approvals: Whether authenticated native channel decisions are supported.
inbound_messages: Whether native inbound messages are accepted.
inbound_reply: Whether authenticated native replies can update canonical conversations.
configuration_valid: Whether the current non-sending configuration check passed.
issues: Safe configuration issues that need operator attention.
diagnostic: Non-sending configuration and identity diagnostic projection.
provider_acceptance: Transport acceptance evidence, separate from an attributed reply.
qualification: Recorded qualification evidence level; configuration alone is not a live round trip.
callbacks: Safe callback URLs and verification requirements.
manifest: Safe provider application manifest for setup.
steps: Ordered setup actions supported by this provider.
sends: Whether a preview itself sends anything; dispatch preview returns false.
next_cursor: Opaque next-page cursor. Continue even when the current items array is empty.
items: Authorized records returned by this page.
filters: Supported exact collection filters, not arbitrary SQL or JSON selectors.
search: Optional text search, at most 200 characters.
cursor: Opaque continuation token, scoped to the same actor, workspace and query; expires after 24 hours.
next_manager: Existing participant to manage the chat when the current manager leaves.
share_history: Explicitly disclose earlier history to additions. False by default.
request: Nested requested-decision input or canonical request in a batch result.
replacement: New pending request; future decisions use this ID.
operations: Map of action names to currently allowed booleans. Actual mutation checks again.
request_version: Request version observed during capability evaluation.
hidden_recipients: Resolved recipients whose details the caller cannot view.
count: Number of recipients resolved by this preview.
collection: One of the documented query collections.
after: Last committed canonical event sequence. Default 0 starts from retained visible events; checkpoint only after applying each event.
approval: Attach a typed approval request to the initial shared chat message. False by default.
base64: Base64-encoded file bytes. MCP transfers are limited to 64 KiB.
base_url: Engine origin, including scheme and optional port. No embedded credentials.
callback_query: Native Telegram callback query object, verified against the connection and linked person.
checks: Concrete subject/action/target checks for a non-saving policy-role preview.
contacts: Authorized contact observations, including available operations and delivery route evidence.
delivery_cursor: Opaque next-page cursor for request trace delivery evidence; empty starts the first page.
descriptor: Optional exact Action descriptor used to evaluate conditional permission, not an executed action.
file: Multipart form field containing one file; 1 byte through 5 MiB for HTTP/SDK uploads.
http: Go HTTP client/transport override. New uses a 20-second timeout; contexts can impose a shorter deadline.
idempotency-key: Saved nonempty operation identity for a retryable creation write; keep body and key identical.
idempotency_key: MCP operation identity. Persist it across unknown results; use a new key only for new intent.
left: True when the membership operation removed the caller from the shared conversation.
role: Policy role object to preview or inspect; separate from an agent_role directory group.
roles: Effective policy-role assignments with direct/group provenance.
stream: Use 1 for text/event-stream; omit for a bounded JSON event page.
update_id: Telegram update identity used for canonical duplicate handling.
wait_ms: Optional inbox long-poll wait in milliseconds; the SDK run loop uses 15000.
x-beepgrid-event-id: Unique signed webhook event identity; stable across identical retries.
x-beepgrid-signature: Webhook HMAC signature over the documented timestamp and raw body.
x-beepgrid-timestamp: Signed webhook timestamp used for replay protection.
x-signature-ed25519: Discord Ed25519 signature over timestamp and raw body, verified using the application public key.
x-signature-timestamp: Discord request timestamp included in signature verification.
x-slack-request-timestamp: Slack timestamp included in v0 signature verification and replay protection.
x-slack-signature: Slack v0 HMAC signature verified with the connection signing secret.
x-telegram-bot-api-secret-token: Telegram webhook secret token configured for this connection.
base64_data: Base64-encoded file bytes, bounded by the MCP transfer limit.
-: Local SDK field; not serialized on the JSON wire.
signal: Optional AbortSignal for stopping this local event stream; does not cancel durable requests.
subject: Authorized subject projection of the access inspection.
context_hash: Digest of the exact shared key, title, body and choices used for reuse eligibility.
question: Original informational question title, retained with the published answer.
author_id: Identity that supplied the original informational answer.
publisher_id: Identity whose current publication authority must remain valid for reuse.
invalidated: Whether this published informational answer has been explicitly invalidated.
source_request: Canonical question request from which this answer was published.
application_id: Immutable Discord application ID for the configured connection.
basis: Recorded authorization basis for this access projection; not a transferable grant.
bot_id: Provider-native bot identity for the configured application.
destination_id: One configured delivery destination to receive this explicit connection test.
issuer: Exact OIDC issuer URL used with the immutable subject; email matching alone is not identity linking.
plan_id: Saved Coordinator plan ID; confirmation accepts this server-owned plan, not arbitrary replacement instructions.
prefix: Permitted enrollment namespace prefix for a bounded launcher.
team_id: Immutable Slack workspace/team ID for the linked account.
user_id: Immutable provider user ID; not the display name or email.
ask: Whether the subject may initiate a requested reply to this contact.
before: Whether the check is allowed under the current effective role grants.
check: The concrete subject, action, target and optional conditions being simulated.
currency: Optional currency code used to constrain a bound business action.
deliveries: Paginated transport evidence; continue using its own next_cursor.
executions: Paginated authenticated executor reports, separate from transport delivery.
from: The agent that declared this blocking communication dependency.
max_amount_minor: Optional maximum action amount in minor currency units.
permitted: Whether current contact and route policy permits this route.
person: Person identity projection; present only for a person caller.
reason: Human-readable explanation of the current policy or routing result.
routes: Visible route projections; no destination secrets or installation credentials.
service: Software service projection; present only for a service caller.
to: The individual agent whose reply is blocking the requester.
changes: Keyword fields to update on a credential, such as name, expires_at, never_expires or permissions. Supply the observed version separately.
clear_permissions: Remove the credential-specific permission restriction. This does not grant permissions absent from the underlying identity.
connection_name: Human-readable label for this Agent runtime connection.
credential: Non-secret credential metadata returned with a newly rotated bearer token.
credential_id: Stable credential identifier. It is not the bearer token.
default: Recipient default channel policy; null preserves existing destination-based routing.
destinations: Recipient-owned delivery destination IDs in preference order. An empty list keeps delivery in the workspace only.
followup_seconds: Delay before trying the next channel for an unanswered question or approval after provider acceptance. Zero disables follow-ups; new delays are 5 to 900 seconds.
last_used_at: Most recently recorded authenticated use, or null. Updates are throttled and are not an exact per-request audit trail.
never_expires: Explicitly request a non-expiring credential. Cannot be combined with an expiry or renewable worker lease.
overlap_seconds: How long the previous token remains usable after rotation, from zero to 86400 seconds. Defaults to 3600.
overrides: Ordered sender-specific delivery preferences. An exact Agent match precedes matching Agent roles, then the recipient default.
owner_name: Display name of the identity that owns the credential.
parent_credential_id: Credential that enrolled this worker, when applicable; used for optional worker revocation with the parent.
permissions: Optional credential-specific restriction to read, message, request, respond, execute or manage. Underlying identity permissions still apply.
policy: Channel delivery policy. It changes delivery destinations without granting contact or decision authority.
previous_until: Deadline for the previous token during rotation overlap, or null when no previous token remains valid.
renewable: Use a renewable 24-hour worker lease bounded by the supplied hard expiry. Renewal never extends the hard deadline.
renewable_until: Hard deadline for a renewable worker credential, or null when it is not renewable.
revoke_workers: Also revoke worker credentials enrolled through this credential.
revoked: Whether the credential has been revoked and can no longer authenticate.
source: Sender selector for a channel override: an exact Agent or an Agent role group.
token_hint: Non-secret token suffix used to identify a credential. It cannot authenticate.
anycast_id: Stable Anycast dispatch ID. The runtime releases its reservation after processing, never on transport acknowledgement.
anycast_role_id: Agent role whose one selected member receives this dispatch. Membership does not grant authority.
role_name: Display name of the addressed agent role.
cancelled: True after queued work was cancelled. This does not stop assigned execution.
completed: True after the assigned runtime released its reservation. Not evidence of business execution success.
input: The saved caller input for this durable dispatch.
anycast: Optional host-owned capacity advertisement. A model should never be prompted to generate it.
restricted: Whether only the selected Agents and current Agent role members may send to this Slack channel. This never grants contact or decision authority.
allowed: Agent and Agent role targets permitted by a restricted channel allowlist. An empty list with restricted=true blocks all Agents.
channels: One bounded page of Slack channels the configured bot has joined. Follow next_cursor even if this filtered page is empty.
